The second season of the American [[situation comedy]] [[television series]], ''[[The Office (American TV series)|The Office]]'', premiered in the United States on [[NBC]] on September 20, 2005, and ended on May 11, 2006.  The season had 22 episodes, including its first 40-minute "super-sized" episode.  ''The Office'' is an American adaptation of the [[The Office (British TV series)|British TV series]], and is presented in a [[mockumentary]] format, documenting the daily lives of office employees in the [[Scranton, Pennsylvania]], branch of the fictitious [[Dunder Mifflin|Dunder Mifflin Paper Company]]. The season stars [[Steve Carell]], [[Rainn Wilson]], [[John Krasinski]], [[Jenna Fischer]], and [[B. J. Novak]], with supporting performances from [[Melora Hardin]], [[David Denman]], [[Leslie David Baker]], [[Brian Baumgartner]], [[Kate Flannery]], [[Angela Kinsey]], [[Oscar Nunez]], and [[Phyllis Smith]].

Beginning with "[[The Dundies]]", the second season further explored the threat of company downsizing. It also introduced new characters while developing those who had been less fleshed out the previous season—especially that of [[Dwight Schrute]] ([[Rainn Wilson]]). [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]] ([[Steve Carell]]) soon starts a relationship with his boss [[Jan Levinson]] ([[Melora Hardin]]), and [[Pam Beesly]] ([[Jenna Fischer]]) and [[Jim Halpert]]'s ([[John Krasinski]]) relationship becomes one of the focal points of the season. Their compatibility becomes more obvious as Jim's feelings for Pam continue to grow, while she struggles with her relationship with warehouse worker [[Roy Anderson (The Office)|Roy Anderson]] ([[David Denman]]).

Season two of ''The Office'' aired on Tuesdays in the United States at 9:30 p.m. from September 20, 2005, to December 6, 2005. The timeslot changed to Thursdays at 9:30 p.m. from January 5, 2006, to May 11, 2006. The season was a ratings success, bolstered by Carell's success in the 2005 film ''[[The 40-Year-Old Virgin]]''. The season also received widespread acclaim from critics. The second season was released in a four-disc DVD boxset in [[DVD region code#Region codes and countries|Region 1]] on September 12, 2006, and in [[DVD region code#Region codes and countries|Region 2]] on January 28, 2008. The DVD set contained all 22 episodes, as well as commentaries from creators, writers, actors, and directors on some of the episodes, while also containing [[deleted scenes]] from all of the episodes. It was released by [[Universal Studios Home Entertainment]].

== Production ==

The second season of ''The Office'' was produced by [[Reveille Productions]] and Deedle-Dee Productions, both in association with [[NBC Universal Television Studio]]s. The show is based on the British series created by [[Ricky Gervais]] and [[Stephen Merchant]] (who also serve as [[executive producer]]s of the American version).<ref name="GreenLight">{{cite news|last=Wood|first=David|title=American Office Gets Green Light|url=https://www.theguardian.com/media/2004/may/18/broadcasting.internationalnews|access-date=September 28, 2012|newspaper=[[The Guardian]]|date=May 18, 2004}}</ref><ref name="DVD4"/> This season was produced by [[Greg Daniels]], who also served as its [[showrunner]]. Returning writers included Daniels, [[Larry Wilmore]], [[Michael Schur]], [[Mindy Kaling]], [[Paul Lieberstein]], and [[B. J. Novak]]. New writers for the season included story editors [[Lee Eisenberg]] and [[Gene Stupnitsky]], consulting producer [[Jennifer Celotta]], and series star, [[Steve Carell]], who wrote the season finale, "[[Casino Night]]".<ref name="DVD4"/><ref name="DVD2">{{cite AV media notes |title=The Office: The Complete First Season |title-link=The Office (American season 1) |first=Ken |last=Kwapis |type=DVD |display-authors=etal|publisher=[[Universal Television|Universal]] |location=[[Los Angeles]] }}</ref><ref>{{cite interview |last=Daniels |first=Greg |title=Casino Night |type=DVD commentary track |publisher=[[Universal Television|Universal]] |location=[[Los Angeles]] |date=2006 |work=The Office: The Complete Second Season}}</ref>

In total, eight different individuals directed the season's 22 episodes. Four of those directors{{Em dash}}[[Bryan Gordon]], [[Ken Kwapis]], [[Ken Whittingham]], and Daniels{{Em dash}}had directed episodes during the show's [[The Office (American season 1)|first season]]. For [[Dennie Gordon]], [[Paul Feig]], [[Victor Nelli, Jr.]], and [[Charles McDougall]], season two marked their directorial debuts on the show.<ref name="DVD4"/><ref name="DVD2"/> In contrast to the previous season, which had been shot in an actual office building, this season of ''The Office'' was mainly filmed on a studio set at Valley Center Studios in [[Van Nuys]], [[California]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Glassman |first=Thea |date=March 19, 2020 |title=How the Remarkably Unremarkable World of Dunder Mifflin Was Built |url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/the-office-anniversary-dunder-mifflin-set-design |access-date=January 6, 2025 |website=Architectural Digest |language=en-US}}</ref>

Despite low ratings from the first season of the show, NBC renewed ''The Office'' for a second season. Originally, six episodes were ordered, but NBC later ordered an additional seven.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBC Gives Bonus to 'The Office'|work=[[Zap2it]]|publisher=[[Tribune Media Services]]|date=September 29, 2005}}</ref> In early November, NBC again expanded the season by ordering three more episodes,<ref>{{cite news|title=NBC May Make More 'Office' Space|work=[[Zap2it]]|publisher=[[Tribune Media Services]]|date=November 4, 2005}}</ref> before ordering a full season of 22 episodes in January 2006.<ref>{{cite press release|title=NBC Renews Comedy Karma with "My Name Is Earl" and Works in "The Office" for Full-Season Orders of 22 Episodes Each for 2006-07|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2006/01/22/nbc-renews-comedy-karma-with-my-name-is-earl-and-works-in-the-office-for-full-season-orders-of-22-episodes-each-for-2006-07-20385/20060122nbc02/|publisher=NBC|date=January 22, 2006|access-date=September 28, 2012}}</ref>

== Cast ==
{{see also|List of The Office (American TV series) characters}}
''The Office'' employed an [[ensemble cast]]. Most of the main characters, and some supporting ones, are based on characters from the British version of ''The Office''. While these characters normally have the same attitudes and perceptions as their British counterparts, the roles have been redesigned to better fit the American show. The show featured a large cast size, many of whom were known for their [[Improvisation|improvisational]] work.<ref name="office-original">{{cite web |last1=Gilbert |first1=Holly |date=November 1, 2020 |title=The Office US Vs. UK Versions: Differences Explained |url=https://screenrant.com/office-us-vs-uk-versions-differences-explained/ |access-date=December 18, 2025 |website=[[Screen Rant]]}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Glassman |first=Thea |date=March 19, 2020 |title=How the Remarkably Unremarkable World of Dunder Mifflin Was Built |url=https://www.architecturaldigest.com/story/the-office-anniversary-dunder-mifflin-set-design |access-date=January 6, 2025 |website=Architectural Digest |language=en-US}}</ref>  

===Main===
* [[Steve Carell]] as [[Michael Scott (The Office)|Michael Scott]], regional manager of the Dunder Mifflin Scranton Branch. Loosely based on [[David Brent]], Gervais' character in the British version,<ref>{{cite news|last=Stanley|first=Alessandra|title=Jolly Good Show Or Was It?; On TV, Attitude Is More Important Than the Way the Vowels Sound|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9800EFD81F30F93BA35757C0A9619C8B63&scp=20&sq=the+office+carell&st=nyt|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=September 28, 2012|date=April 8, 2007}}</ref> Scott is a dim-witted and lonely man, who attempts to win friends as the office comedian, usually making himself look bad in the process.  
* [[Rainn Wilson]] as [[Dwight Schrute]], who, based upon [[Gareth Keenan]], is the assistant to the regional manager, although the character frequently fails to include "to the" in his title.<ref>{{cite news|last=Rooney|first=Brian|title=The Man Behind 'The Office's' Favorite Suck-Up, Dwight Schrute|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Nightline/story?id=3566414&page=1#.UGYDWGjd7ww|newspaper=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]]|publisher=[[American Broadcasting Company]]|access-date=September 28, 2012|date=September 7, 2007}}</ref> 
* [[John Krasinski]] as [[Jim Halpert]], a sales representative and prankster, who is based upon [[Tim Canterbury]], and is in love with Pam Beesly, the receptionist.<ref>{{cite news|last=Carter|first=Bill|title='The Office' Transfers to a New Cubicle|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/03/20/arts/television/20Cart.html?pagewanted=2&_r=1&sq=John%20Krasinski&st=nyt&oref=slogin&scp=2|access-date=September 28, 2012|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 20, 2005}}</ref> 
* [[Jenna Fischer]] as [[Pam Beesly]], who is based on [[Dawn Tinsley]], is shy, but is often a cohort with Jim in his pranks on Dwight.<ref name=ny3>{{cite news|last=Alessandra|first=Stanley|title=An American-Style ''Office'' With a Boss From Heck|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/03/24/arts/television/24stan.html?scp=1&sq=Jenna+Fischer&st=nyt|access-date=September 28, 2012|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=March 24, 2005}}</ref> 
* [[B. J. Novak]] as [[Ryan Howard (The Office)|Ryan Howard]], who is a [[temporary worker]].<ref name=ny3/>

===Starring===
Halfway through the season, eight of the show's recurring guest stars were promoted to series regulars and credited just after the main titles and before the writers and producers.<ref name="angela">Kinsey, Angela (Writer). 2006. "Performance Review" [Commentary track], ''The Office'' Season Two (US/NBC Version) [DVD], Los Angeles, CA: [[Universal Television|Universal]].</ref>

* [[Melora Hardin]] as [[Jan Levinson]], Michael's main love interest and vice president of regional sales.
* [[David Denman]] as Roy Anderson, a warehouse worker and Pam's [[fiance|fiancé]].
* [[Leslie David Baker]] as Stanley Hudson, a grumpy salesman.
* [[Brian Baumgartner]] as [[Kevin Malone]], a dim-witted accountant.
* [[Kate Flannery]] as Meredith Palmer, the promiscuous supplier relations rep.
* [[Angela Kinsey]] as [[Angela Martin]], a judgmental accountant, who also serves as Dwight’s love interest.
* [[Oscar Nunez]] as [[Oscar Martinez (The Office)|Oscar Martinez]], an intelligent accountant, who is also gay.
* [[Phyllis Smith]] as Phyllis Lapin, a motherly saleswoman.<ref name=tguidecast>{{cite web|title=The Office Cast and Details|url=http://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/the-office/cast/191831|work=[[TV Guide]]|access-date=September 30, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120130215641/https://www.tvguide.com/tvshows/the-office/cast/191831/|archive-date=January 30, 2012}}</ref>

===Recurring===
* [[Mindy Kaling]] as [[Kelly Kapoor]], the pop culture-obsessed customer service representative.
* [[Paul Lieberstein]] as Toby Flenderson, the sad-eyed human resources representative.
* [[Creed Bratton]] as Creed Bratton, the office's strange quality assurance officer.
* [[Craig Robinson (actor)|Craig Robinson]] as Darryl Philbin, the warehouse manager.
* Devon Abner as Devon White, a supplier relations representative.
* [[Hugh Dane]] as Hank Tate, the building's security guard.
* [[David Koechner]] as Todd Packer, a rude and offensive traveling salesman, who’s Michael’s best friend.
* [[Nancy Carell|Nancy Walls]] as Carol Stills, a real estate agent.
* [[Amy Adams]] as Katy Moore, a handbag saleswoman and Jim’s girlfriend.
* [[Bobby Ray Shafer]] as Bob Vance, Phyllis' boyfriend, who runs Vance Refrigeration.
* [[Andy Buckley]] as [[David Wallace (The Office)|David Wallace]], the new CFO of Dunder Mifflin.<ref name=tguidecast/>

== Broadcast and reception ==

===Ratings===

{{image frame
|content={{#chart:OfficeUS2ratings.chart}}
|width = 500
|caption = Ratings for each episode of ''The Office'' that aired this season.{{ref|cite|i}}
}}

The season premiere, "[[The Dundies]]" was viewed by 9.0 million viewers, a drastic increase from the first season finale "[[Hot Girl (The Office)|Hot Girl]]", which was viewed by only 4.8 million viewers.<ref name="boysngirls-2" /> As the season progressed, the success of Carell's hit summer movie ''[[The 40-Year-Old Virgin]]'' and online sales of episodes via the [[iTunes]] store helped the show to garner viewers.<ref name=chicagosales>{{cite news|last=Ryan|first=Maureen|title=''Office'' Promotions Pay Off in a Big Way|url=http://featuresblogs.chicagotribune.com/entertainment_tv/2006/02/office_workers_.html|newspaper=[[Chicago Tribune]]|date=February 23, 2006|access-date=March 20, 2008|quote=Because of the relationship we have with [the feature-film division of NBC Universal], within the company we knew that Steve had been identified as a big star and we'd be crazy to let him go,' said Angela Bromstad, president of NBC Universal Television Studio, the production company behind ''The Office''. Hence the second-season pickup of the show.|archive-date=November 7, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161107191911/http://featuresblogs.chicagotribune.com/entertainment_tv/2006/02/office_workers_.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> The increase in viewership led NBC to move the series to the "[[Must See TV]]" Thursday night in January 2006, where ratings continued to grow.<ref name=hollywood/><ref>{{cite book|title=TV Year: The Prime Time 2005-2006 Season|volume=1|date=2007|last=Muir|first=John Kenneth|publisher=[[Bloomsbury|Bloomsbury Academic]]|isbn=9781557836847|page=98}}</ref> The season hit a ratings peak with the twelfth episode, "[[The Injury]]", which was viewed by 10.3 million viewers.<ref name=injuryratings>{{cite news|last=Collins|first=Scott|title=NBC Enjoyed Thursday Night|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=January 13, 2006}}</ref> The season finale, "[[Casino Night]]"—which was also the show's first forty-minute-long episode—was viewed by 7.6 million viewers.<ref name="boysngirls-2" /><ref name="NBCRelease">{{cite web|title=NBC Celebrates May with Series Finales of Coveted Classics|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2006/04/20/nbc-celebrates-may-with-series-finales-of-coveted-classics-the-west-wing-and-will-and-grace-and-offers-fans-a-super-sized-thursday-night-of-comedies-the-miniseries-105-apocalypseand-cant-miss-season-finales-21137/20060420nbc02/|publisher=The Futon Critic|access-date=September 28, 2012|date=April 20, 2006}}</ref>

By the end of the 2005–06 season, ''The Office'' tied with ''[[20/20 (US television series)|20/20]]'' as the 67th most-watched show of the year. It averaged eight&nbsp;million viewers, and scored a 4.0/10 in the [[Nielsen ratings]], meaning that on average four percent of households were tuned in at any given moment and ten percent of all televisions in use at the time were tuned into the program. The show received dramatic gains in viewers from the previous year, up forty percent in total viewers and up sixty percent in viewers ages 18–49.<ref name="hollywood">{{cite news|url=http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr/television/feature_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1002576393|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20060722011251/http://www.hollywoodreporter.com/thr/television/feature_display.jsp?vnu_content_id=1002576393|archive-date=July 22, 2006 |title=2005–06 Primetime Wrap|newspaper=[[The Hollywood Reporter]]|access-date=April 12, 2008}}</ref> A year-end report by NBC noted, "''The Office'' was the fastest-growing series on television this season versus last ... ''The Office'' grew by 60 percent this season in adults 18{{en dash}}49 (to an average 4.0 rating from a 2.5 the prior season)."<ref>{{cite press release |date=May 23, 2006 |title=May 23, 2006 Press Release (the 2005{{en dash}} 2006 Season) |url=https://www.officetally.com/the-office-nielsen-ratings/2 |publisher=[[NBC]] |access-date=December 6, 2017}}</ref>

===Reviews===
[[File:Steve Carell November 2014.jpg|upright|thumb|left|[[Steve Carell]] received awards for both acting and writing.|alt=A man with black hair, Steve Carell, is standing in a tux. He is looking towards the camera and smiles.]]

The second season of ''The Office'' was released largely to critical acclaim and commercial success. Francis Rizzo III of [[DVD Talk]] wrote that the British version "can't hold a candle to the American" version during this season, due to the show coming "into its own, becoming the best half-hour show on TV."<ref name=dvdtalk/> Furthermore, Rizzo wrote that the season was filled with "fantastically real characters" as well as "one of the best-handled romances in TV history".<ref name=dvdtalk>{{cite web|last=Rizzo III|first=Francis|title=The Office – Season Two|url=https://www.dvdtalk.com/reviews/23501/office-season-two-the/|work=[[DVD Talk]]|publisher=[[Internet Brands]]|access-date=September 28, 2012|date=September 12, 2006}}</ref> Eric Goldman of ''[[IGN]]'' noted that season two transformed ''The Office'' "from a very funny show into a truly brilliant show".<ref name=ign/> Goldman praised the world-building of the season, writing that it "does a wonderful job of developing the rest of the staff of Dunder-Mifflin {{sic}}, something the UK version could never do to this extent".<ref name=ign/> He ultimately gave it a ten out of ten score.<ref name=ign>{{cite web|last=Goldman|first=Eric|title=The Office – Season Two (US/2005)|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2006/09/13/the-office-season-two-us2005|work=[[IGN]]|publisher=[[News Corporation (1980–2013)|News Corporation]]|access-date=September 28, 2012|date=September 13, 2006}}</ref> Josh Wolk, an ''[[Entertainment Weekly]]'' television critic, said that the show has "perfecting workaday moments so hilariously and relatably awkward that it makes viewers both laugh and cringe".<ref>{{cite magazine|last=Wolk|first=Josh|title=Take This Job and Love It|url=http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1159867,00.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070325203259/http://www.ew.com/ew/article/0,,1159867,00.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 25, 2007|magazine=[[Entertainment Weekly]]|publisher=[[Time Inc.|Time, Inc]]|access-date=September 28, 2012|date=February 17, 2006}}</ref>

The season was also a commercial success. Midway through the season, a deal was made with [[Apple Inc|Apple]] to offer the show's episodes for download through its iTunes store.<ref name=chicagosales/> This action, in turn, led to many fans buying the series before the DVD set was released. For some time, "[[The Carpet (The Office)|The Carpet]]", the season's fourteenth episode, was the second most-downloaded episode of a television show in the store,<ref>{{cite news|last=Collins|first=Scott|title=Office party - Carell show gathers steam for NBC in 2nd season|access-date=June 13, 2012|url=http://docs.newsbank.com.www2.lib.ku.edu:2048/s/InfoWeb/aggdocs/NewsBank/10F8BDCF7B6B6918/0F8479522BD09CA1?s_lang=en-US|newspaper=[[The Journal Gazette]]|publisher=The Journal Gazette Co|date=February 2, 2006|page=3D}} {{subscription required}}</ref> and by early January 2006, episodes from ''The Office'' occupied ten of the twenty slots in the iTunes list of most popular downloads.<ref>Roberts, V.E. (January 4, 2006). [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/media/the-office-hits-top-spot-in-us-download-charts-6112739.html ''The Office'' hits top spot in US download charts] ''[[The Independent]]''. Retrieved June 23, 2008</ref> In 2006, after the release of the DVD, the second season was the seventeenth highest selling DVD on [[Amazon.com|Amazon]] that year.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amazon.com/gp/feature.html?docId=1000022091|title=The Customers' Favorites: Top 100 DVD Bestsellers|publisher=[[Amazon.com|Amazon]]|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090416080729/http://www.amazon.com/gp/feature.html?ie=UTF8&docId=1000022091|archive-date=April 16, 2009}}</ref>

=== Accolades ===
The second season of ''The Office'' received five nominations at the [[58th Primetime Emmy Awards]], and won the award for [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Comedy Series|Outstanding Comedy Series]]. Other nominations included [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series|Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series]] for [[Steve Carell]], [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series|Outstanding Writing for a Comedy Series]] for [[Michael Schur]] (for the episode "[[Christmas Party (The Office)|Christmas Party]]"), and [[Primetime Emmy Award for Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series|Outstanding Single-Camera Picture Editing for a Comedy Series]] for both "Christmas Party" (edited by David Rogers) and "[[Booze Cruise (The Office)|Booze Cruise]]" (edited by [[Dean Holland]]).<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.nbc.com/movies-specials-more/Emmys_2006/nominees.shtml |title=The 58th Primetime Emmy Awards and Creative Arts Emmys Nominations |access-date=June 22, 2008 |publisher=[[NBC]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121102105653/http://www.nbc.com/movies-specials-more/Emmys_2006/nominees.shtml == DVD release ==
The second season of ''The Office'' was released by Universal Studios Home Entertainment as a four-disc Region 1 DVD box set on September 12, 2006.<ref>{{cite web |title=The Office: Season Two DVD DigiPack |url=https://www.blu-ray.com/dvd/The-Office-Season-Two-DVD/12831/ |publisher=[[Blu-ray|Blu-ray.com]] |access-date=January 27, 2026}}</ref> The set includes all 22 episodes presented in a 1.78:1 aspect ratio with Dolby Digital 5.1 Surround sound and optional English and Spanish subtitles. The release also included an array of bonus materials, including audio commentaries for 10 episodes, as well as deleted scenes from every episode of the season. Additional special features include the "Faces of Scranton" music video, a series of fake [[Public service announcement|Public Service Announcements]], the "Steve on Steve" featurette, a blooper reel, "The Accountants" [[Webisode|webisodes]], and a promotional spot for the 2006 Winter Olympics.<ref name="DVD4">{{cite AV media notes |title=The Office: The Complete Second Season |last=Daniels|first=Greg|type=DVD |display-authors=etal|publisher=[[Universal Television|Universal]] |location=[[Los Angeles]]}}</ref>
